solution: For each original value x, an element can end at x*2^k with cost k, or floor(x/2^k) with cost k for k >= 1; any mixed sequence has the same net exponent but no smaller cost, so mixed operations are unnecessary. Generate all positive reachable values at most sum with their minimum costs, then run a multiple-choice knapsack DP where dp[s] is the minimum operations needed to form sum s. Each element contributes at most one transformed value, or is skipped, and transitions use a fresh copy of the previous DP layer. The answer is dp[sum] if finite, otherwise -1; the complexity is O(n * sum * (log sum + log max(nums))) time and O(sum) space.
